correctness.rationale: For noncollinear circle nodes the centered sample zonotope has full-dimensional image and its gauge equals the minimal relative weight radius. Strong LP duality gives the support as the sum of deviations from a projected median. Each projection-order chamber has a linear support, so its quotient with the linear first moment maximizes at a chord-normal boundary. Uniform SLLN on a compact Lipschitz (direction, offset) family gives support/m -> 2/pi; the 2D CLT with covariance I/2 then yields the Rayleigh CDF 1-exp(-4c^2/pi^2). The independent LP solver matched the finite chord formula on 204 seeded random instances; numerical tests are corroborative only.

value.rationale: For the natural first nonconstant trigonometric quadrature space under iid circle nodes, the bound from the motivating literature leaves the sharp constant and critical success probability open. The finite chord-normal formula decides exact near-equal-weight feasibility on an actual node set with finitely many directions and the limiting Rayleigh law gives the exact probability of strict positivity at tolerance c/sqrt(m). Both metrics directly address precision budgets in random positive quadrature, not an arbitrary slice or a known table recomputation.
